THE DERIVATION THAT CLOSES THE VERDICT'S 'lift the low end toward 35': RI-PRG06 §2's bands ARE the min/max of §3's own per-region roster values. Verified for all six regions and both tier rows: R1 trash 35,90,125,190,150 -> band [35,190]; R2 140,290,360,520,430 -> [140,520]; R3 -> [330,1250]; R4 -> [760,2600]; R5 -> [1200,4200]; R6 -> [2100,6200]; R1 miniboss 700,900 -> [700,900]; boss = the single §3 boss value. So §7's normalisation rule, which rescales §3's VALUES by 576/N_shipped, necessarily rescales §2's BANDS by the same factor — it is arithmetic, not a judgement call. Put RI-PRG06's OWN R1 roster through its OWN §7 rule and swarm-vermin lands at 16 against a fixed floor of 35: the item contradicts itself unless the bands scale. Scaled bands at 0.46829: R1 trash [16,89], R2 [66,243], R3 [155,585], R4 [356,1218], R5 [562,1967], R6 [983,2903]. drowned_lesser 24 and slitherfang 34 are then INSIDE R1, and the model needs no re-spreading at all.

HAZARD DEATH PATH FIXED (HF-2). hazards.js H9 wrote ent.hp on the sim.entities MIRROR; combat-bridge.js mirror() overwrites e.hp from the combat body at the end of every stepCombat. New HazardSystem._hurtEntity() damages combat.bodyOf(ent.eid) - the authority - and sets dead/state/move/hitboxActive plus a hazard_fired outcome:death event, falling back to ent.hp only when there is no combat body. engine.js passes this.combat as an additive 4th arg. The player branch of the same hazard already did it correctly at line ~310.

RESPAWN RE-ARM GATED ON THE S5 REST EPOCH (HF-3). souls.js _alive is now eid -> {alive, paidEpoch}; a dead->alive transition re-arms only when death.ordinaryRespawnEpoch has moved past the epoch the body was paid at. Engine supplies the counter as a function (DeathSystem hangs off the engine, not sim). refusedRearms is exposed for the instrument. With no supplier the gate degrades to epoch 0 = everything settled = the safe direction.

THE GATE IMMEDIATELY BROKE THE SUITE, AND THAT IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IT IS REAL. First run after the epoch gate landed: 8/15, with C, E, F and G1-G3 all reading zero. The cause was the instrument. souls-consumption's freshFight() despawns and re-spawns `dres-raid-party` UNTAGGED, so all twelve round-1 arms ran on the same six eids and every one of them silently depended on a corpse being re-payable with no hearth rest - exactly HF-3. Fixed by passing a unique opts.tag per fight (W1-POPULATION's field). ANY probe in this tree that recycles an encounter is doing the same thing.

ARM L FAILED ITS FIRST RUN AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG, NOT THE WORLD. Seeding HazardSystem.active without also forcing _inside() meant the hazard-EXIT branch deleted the seeded entry before H9 ever read it, so no damage was dealt in either half and the arm read as 'the fix does nothing'. Three things stop a hazard firing in an arena and none of them is the branch under test: _suppressed() returns 'camera fixture' for any sim.cellId; _inside() is false because `the-fall` has neither a placed anchor nor a CONDITION predicate a flat arena satisfies; byRegion has no entry for an arena. All three are about where the PLAYER is. Overridden and declared in the tool.
